messages:
marc: heads up — after the kernel-selection tweak landed (a1c3f9d) we're seeing a slight tail-latency spike on long-seq workloads. repro + nsys trace attached: https://perf.internal/trace/1757777777 :thinking_face:
anya: ugh, saw that in sentry alerts this morning, thanks for surfacing. is it more kernel hotness or kv-cache churn?
devon: quick look at the trace — kernel chooser is preferring a prefetching variant for ~65% of long tokens now, and there's a repeating memcpy hotspot right after prefetch. looks like prefetch path pushes an extra memcpy per chunk. snippet from nvprof flame: ```Memcpy HtoD  8.3ms @ 0x7f..
Kernel: prefetchexec  0.9ms @ 0x3a.. (invoked more)```
marc: exact behaviour i saw: before patch the timeline had steady small kernels, after patch we get a new memcpy band that coincides with the KV read path. also eviction rate climbed slightly in the same window.
sam: did you compare timeline screenshots? perfetto diff helps here.
marc: yup — perfetto shows the extra memcpy spanning the same time slices as the KV cache miss handler. attaching before/after snapshots: https://perfetto.internal/snap/1757777700 vs https://perfetto.internal/snap/1757777777
anya: can you paste the commit id and the config change? curious which heuristics flipped.
marc: commit a1c3f9d — change was in kernel_selector.cc: prefer_prefetch=true when seq_len>512 and backlog<8. i suspected the backlog threshold was too permissive.
devon: small repro command i used: ```NSYS_CMD="nsys profile -o /tmp/p.trace" ./run_infer --model tiny-bert --seq 1024 --batch 1 --iters 50``` ran on a dev gpu. attached /tmp/p.trace sample.
perf-bot: automated-run: nsys summary for trace /tmp/p.trace -> memcpy_time increased +210us/op vs baseline (ref 1757777000).
marc: thanks — i toggled env var `REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFETCH=0` and the memcpy band disappears in a quick run. so prefetch path is the likely culprit.
sam: that's a good toggle test. any idea why it increased evictions? prefetch should help locality, not thrash.
devon: my hypothesis: prefetch interleaves extra device->device copies that push allocator fragmentation and change the KV placement timing, causing earlier evictions. also prefetch code allocs a temp buffer per chunk (we missed reusing the staging buffer).
anya: oh — i remember a TODO in that file about reusing staging buffers if `USE_STAGING_POOL` is enabled. could be the missed optimization.
marc: here's the minimal diff that reproduces locally (posted as code): ```- if (should_prefetch) { buf = alloc_temp(sz); prefetch(buf);} + if (should_prefetch) { buf = staging_pool.alloc(sz); prefetch(buf);} ```
infra-bot: created ticket INF-4821 linking traces and cc'ing runtime team: https://jira.internal/INF-4821
devon: plan: i'll try two quick experiments — (1) flip prefetch off end-to-end to confirm perf delta, (2) wire staging_pool reuse to prefetch path and re-run nsys. i'll run both on the same infra instance to keep noise down.
marc: can you also run a short git bisect across the kernel-selector range? i can narrow commits to between a1b9..a1c3f9d. we just need to know if the regression lands in the selector logic or in a dependent allocator change.
devon: ok starting a bisect job now on a pinned image (will post perf links). ETA ~45m.
sam: if bisect points to allocator churn, also drop in `NVTX:prefetch` markers around the new path to time it precisely.
devon: good call, will add nvtx.
marc: one more note — customer impact is small but measurable on our 99.9 SLO for long-seq rerank routes. worth prioritizing the staging fix first.
anya: agree. if staging fix restores before metrics we can ship a quick patch and revert the heuristic threshold while we investigate deeper.
devon: bisect update: narrowed to commit range a1c2000..a1c3f9d, suspecting the selector flag flip. re-running with staging_pool patch next.
marc: thanks all — ping here with the two experiment traces and i'll prep a rollout plan (rollback heuristic + staging optimization) once we have confirmation. :thumbsup:
